## Questions

Are there archetypes/ personality groups of listeners that can be identified?
Is there some less popular / less well known music that could be more widely appreciated if the right people were exposed to it?

## High level goal and expanded description
The goal is to build a music recommender system based on user's listening habits. This algorithm could serve to help listeners to find new music that they might enjoy, and also could help artists by exposing them to listeners that may enjoy their music.

## Data and motivation
This dataset is based on the subset of users in the #nowplaying dataset who publish their #nowplaying tweets via Spotify. In principle, the dataset holds users, their playlists and the tracks contained in these playlists.
https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/andrewmvd/spotify-playlists

The goal is to build a music recommender system based on users' listening habits. This algorithm could serve to help listeners to find new music that they might enjoy, and also could help artists by exposing them to listeners that may enjoy their music.

The dataset contains the following columns:
"user_id", "artistname", "trackname", "playlistname"
- user_id is a hash of the user's Spotify user name
- artistname is the name of the artist
- trackname is the title of the track and
- playlistname is the name of the playlist that contains this track.

This data does not contain features / tags describing the characteristics of the songs. The approach would be to identify similar listening habits among certain people and recommend music that similar listeners enjoy. This could be in the form of a collaborative filtering algorigthm.

## Weekly "plan of attack"
For this project, graph (network) visuals may be helpful to see clusters of listeners with similar listening habits. Once we are familiar with the data we will begin preprocessing, followed by testing and refining different algorithms. 

Schedule may be updated as project progresses

- 10/26 - Decide on project and put together proposal
- 11/2 - Explore / visualize and understand the data
- 11/9 - Clean and prepare the data
- 11/16 - Try different algorithms and hyperparameter tuning
- 11/23 - Continue refining algorithms / hyperparameters
- 11/30 - Refine final model
- 12/7 - Recap and presentation


## Repository structure and folder `README.md` files
The project repository will be organized into folders like data/, notebooks/, src/, and reports/, each holding the related scripts, notebooks, and documentation. The main README.md  will give an overview of the project, setup instructions, and data details to help anyone get started quickly. Each folder will also have its own short README.md explaining what’s inside and how to use it. This structure keeps everything clean, easy to navigate, and ensures the project can be reproduced without confusion.
